title: Lean4Physics: Comprehensive Reasoning Framework for College-level Physics in Lean4
claim: A unified framework couples a layered, bottom-up formal library and benchmark with an LLM evaluation pipeline that tests whether the library helps.
layout: 2 stacked panels; (a) construction top, (b) evaluation bottom; left-to-right flow
description: The figure has two dashed-border panels. Panel (a), Formal Data Construction, runs left to right. A blue rounded card holds the natural-language statement (condition, question, steps, answer). It feeds green condition and target extraction boxes. These feed a 3D layered block stack: Unit System, SI System, Calculation Support Layer, and physics-domain tiles (Mechanics, Waves, Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics). The 'NL to FL translation with PhysLib' label sits above the stack. Next comes a blue formal Lean statement card with hypothesis and goal. Last is a cylinder database stack listing the physics domains of LeanPhysBench. Panel (b) is the LLM evaluation. Mixed statements on the left go into a column of LLM logos. Those produce Proof 1, 2 and 3 cards that hold Lean code. Orange arrows lead to a Lean logo and Evaluation Results. Blue, green and orange coding separates the stages.
caption: Overview of the \method framework: (a) Benchmark and Library Construction: The benchmark and library are developed using a bottom-up principle. We first establish the foundational units and SI system of \lib, then compose the calculation support, and finally construct the field-related theorems. For the benchmark, NL questions are transformed from a question-answering format to proof problems and subsequently formalized into Lean4 statements. (b) LLM Performance Evaluation: We evaluate the formal physics reasoning capabilities of major open and closed-source LLMs on \bench, both with and without \lib. After inference is completed, Lean4 auto-verification evaluates model performance and highlights the utility of \lib.
abstract: We present **Lean4PHYS**, a comprehensive reasoning framework for college-level physics problems in Lean4. **Lean4PHYS** includes *LeanPhysBench*, a college-level benchmark for formal physics reasoning in Lean4, which contains 200 hand-crafted and peer-reviewed statements derived from university textbooks and physics competition problems. To establish a solid foundation for formal reasoning in physics, we also introduce *PhysLib*, a community-driven repository containing fundamental unit systems and theorems essential for formal physics reasoning. Based on the benchmark and Lean4 repository we composed in **Lean4PHYS**, we report baseline results using major expert Math Lean4 provers and state-of-the-art closed-source models, with the best performance of DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B achieving only 16% and Claude-Sonnet-4 achieving 35%. We also conduct a detailed analysis showing that our *PhysLib* can achieve an average improvement of 11.75% in model performance. This demonstrates the challenging nature of our *LeanPhysBench* and the effectiveness of *PhysLib*. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to provide a physics benchmark in Lean4.
